Added 32 claim-linked evidence entries and added or enriched 13 bibliography entries in this record. Related formulation/stock limitations for this review batch: The parent HTML total-volume heading conflicts with the per-liter-of-seawater procedure/PDF. Expanded recipes retain absolute liquid inputs; no measured final volume or final constituent concentrations are inferred. The enrichment source lists vitamin doses but omits a later vitamin-addition instruction; no missing step is invented. ES Fe formula and Sigma F1513 catalog identity remain unreconciled. Only the source-named ferrous-ammonium-sulfate stock mass is supported; no catalog-based replacement or molar conversion is made. The P-II source permits a cobalt sulfate alternative without an exact replacement mass/hydrate. Only the listed cobalt chloride hexahydrate amount is supported. No exact glycerophosphate-pentahydrate ontology identifier was established. Unsupported sn-glycerol-3-phosphate assertions are removed; the immutable MIM index remains unchanged. Generic lighting, temperature, application and growth claims remain outside this ingredient review; no taxa-media associations are added. The 2/3 PDF copyright notice does not establish a publication year for the live HTML. Supplier pages inspected by the web tool are not full downloaded captures.

preparation_steps.description: Prepare H2O stock solutions at the printed concentrations; autoclave stocks except BaCO3, which is 0.22 um filter-sterilized, and store heavy-metal stocks in the dark.
In a 2 L bottle, combine each solid ingredient or liquid stock and fill to 1 L with purified H2O.
Assemble a sterile sparging apparatus on the 2 L bottle and autoclave the 1 L medium with the apparatus attached.
After cooling, sparge the medium with CO2 for 4 h.
Disconnect CO2, sparge with air for 12-24 h to remove excess CO2, then replace the sparging apparatus with a sterile non-vented cap and store at room temperature.

preparation_steps.description: Mix NH4NO3, KH2PO4, Fe(III)-EDTA, Vitamin mixture, Metal mixture, and Artificial seawater.
Adjust to pH 8.0 with NaOH.
Distribute 20-50 ml aliquots into 120 ml serum bottles and seal with butyl rubber stoppers.
Autoclave at 110 degrees C for 5 min.
Allow the autoclaved medium to stand overnight, then add ethane to 10-50% of the gas phase by volume.

evidence.explanation: Abt et al. 2011 genome report; explicit type-strain growth on DSMZ medium 514 (= this parent medium) at 15C. | Identifiers: DSM 14237; CIP 107446; LMG 21425; INSDC CP002453; BioProject 41529; IMG 2503904003
evidence.snippet: C. algicola IC166T, DSM 14237, was grown in DSMZ medium 514 (BACTO marine broth) at 15C.

evidence.explanation: Han et al. 2009; direct cultivation/growth testing of the type strain on Marine Agar/Broth 2216 (= this parent medium family). | Identifiers: DSM 16069; KCTC 12182; 16S AY520560
evidence.snippet: Colony morphology and temperature growth were determined on marine agar 2216 (Difco), and pH dependence was determined in marine broth 2216 (Difco). Colonies after 7 d at 30C; optimum 30-37C; pH optimum 7.0-8.0.

evidence.explanation: Beyersmann et al. 2013; explicit growth on DSMZ medium 514 / Marine Broth 2216 at 20C.
evidence.snippet: P. caeruleus DSM 24564T was grown in DSMZ medium 514. After incubation for 24 h in marine broth 2216 with shaking, visible growth was observed at 20C but not at 28C (100 rpm).

evidence.explanation: Hollensteiner et al. 2020; medium identity explicitly aliased to this parent record; 30C, 180 rpm, 2 d. | Identifiers: DSM 106830T; KCTC 52469T; NBRC 112431T
evidence.snippet: A single colony was passed for 2 days in Medium 514, explicitly identified as DSMZ Medium 514 Bacto Marine Broth Difco 2216, at 30C and 180 rpm.

evidence.explanation: Stackebrandt et al. 2013; isolation on Marine Agar 2216 (recognizable 2216 formulation under this parent medium family). Agar isolation rather than broth growth. | Identifiers: DSM 19592; KCTC 12518; CGMCC 1.6973
evidence.snippet: J. marina strain En5T was isolated by dilution-plating on marine agar 2216 (Difco).

evidence.explanation: Marteinsson et al. 2010; type strain grown on the half-strength MB1/2 variant of this parent medium (see variant mb_half_strength_marine_broth_2216). Deep-sea isolate; pressure tests at 0.1 and 25 MPa. | Identifiers: DSM 22212T; JCM 15944T
evidence.snippet: MB1/2 defined as DSMZ medium 514 / Bacto Marine Broth Difco 2216 diluted to half strength with water; PRI 2902T grown on agar MB1/2 and in liquid MB1/2; colonies after 4 d at 70C.

variants.name: mb_half_strength_marine_broth_2216
variants.description: MB1/2: DSMZ medium 514 / Bacto Marine Broth (Difco 2216) diluted to half strength with water, used for Rhodothermus profundi and related PRI isolates.
modifications: Marine broth/agar 2216 (DSMZ medium 514) diluted to 0.5x strength with water.
For single-carbon-source assays, peptone and yeast extract omitted from MB1/2 plates (assay variant, not routine MB1/2).
variants.purpose: Half-strength marine broth/agar 2216 used to cultivate slow-growing deep-sea Rhodothermus isolates; recognizable concentration variant, not a separate medium.

evidence.explanation: Marteinsson et al. 2010 defines MB1/2 explicitly as half-strength DSMZ 514 / Bacto Marine Broth 2216.
evidence.snippet: MB1/2 ... diluted to half strength with water; growth on single carbon sources tested on plates containing MB1/2 without peptone and yeast extract.

preparation_steps.description:
Make up to 1 litre with distilled water. pH is adjusted to 6.6.  Autoclave at 15 psi for 
15 minutes.

Add to 1000 ml of distilled water 0.75 g Na2EDTA and the minerals in exactly the 
following sequence:
Filter sterile
Take 1 ml of this solution and add 99 ml Deionised water. Filter sterile.

Site selection for a good soil is very important and for most purposes a soil from 
undisturbed deciduous woodland is best.  Sites to avoid are those showing obvious 
signs of man's activity and particular care should be taken to avoid areas where 
fertilizers, crop sprays or other toxic chemicals may have been used.

A rich loam with good crumb structure should be sought.  Stones, roots and larger 
invertebrates should be removed during an initial sieving through a 1 cm mesh.  The sieved soil should be spread to air dry and hand picked for smaller 
invertebrates and roots.  It should be turned periodically and picked over again.  When dry it may be sieved through a finer mesh (2­4 mm) or stored as it is prior to
use.

Soil is prepared as above.  105 g of air­dried sieved soil and 660 ml of deionized 
water are placed in a 1 litre bottle and autoclaved once at 15 psi for 15 minutes, 
then again after 24 hours.  The contents of the bottle are left to settle (usually for 
at least a week) and then the supernatant is decanted and filtered.  The final pH
should be 7.0 - 8.0.
